5/5 The 33-dodecahedron witness explains a plateau through a 1 + 12 + 20 shell structure.

One central piece, twelve inner centers in icosahedral directions, twenty outer centers in dodecahedral directions. Counts 29-32 retain the same core and omit outer pieces; each outer piece https://t.co/LChFt47p94

mediaDetails.ext_alt_text: Two views of the same certified 33-dodecahedron witness: left shows actual solid poses with translucent teal outer pieces, gold inner pieces, and a purple central piece; right shows the actual centers with explicitly schematic dashed shell guides that do not represent contacts. There is one central piece, 12 inner centers forming a dual icosahedral shell and 20 outer centers forming a dodecahedral shell. Counts 29–33 share certified container edge 3.7470909531576 by omitting outer pieces. The 33-piece near-contact graph has 102 edges and none connects similarly oriented pieces within 5 degrees. Colors denote shell class, not orientation. Feasible construction bounds, not a claim of global optimality.

mediaDetails.ext_alt_text: A comparison of two actual archived patterns. Left: dodecahedra in a dodecahedron at counts 29–33 all have certified edge 3.7470909531576, while occupied volume rises through 55.1%, 57.0%, 58.9%, 60.8%, 62.7%. Right: six octahedra in an octahedron have certified edge 2.0000003674235; seven have 2.5000004286608. The edge rises 25.0% and container volume 95.3%, while occupied volume falls from 75.0% to 44.8%. Values are feasible construction upper bounds and their structural measurements, not proved global optima.
